column1: # PAX6 RNA-seq study and batch inventory.
# THE ONLY FILE YOU EDIT WHEN DATA ARRIVES.
# Columns, tab separated:
#   study        libraries that belong in ONE statistical model, and therefore
#                in one count matrix. Counting is scoped to a study.
#   batch        sequencing batch within that study. Becomes the `batch`
#                covariate. Unique within a study.
#   layout       PE or SE. Determines whether fragments or reads are counted.
#                `auto` until measured -- strand_check.sh reports it.
#   strand       featureCounts -s value: 0, 1, 2, or `auto` until measured.
#                NEVER assume this, not even from the same vendor.
#   trimmed_dir  trimmed FASTQs for this batch ( - if not applicable)
#   mapping_dir  where this batch's BAMs live
# WHY STUDY AND BATCH ARE DIFFERENT COLUMNS
#   Lauderdale_2025 and Lauderdale_2026 are two batches of one study: same
#   alleles, same design, batch fitted as a covariate. GSE183742 is a separate
#   study -- adult cornea from the Duncan lab carrying Pax6^tm1Pgr, not
#   Pax6^Sey-Neu. It is quantified identically so the results are comparable,
#   and modelled separately because the allele differs. Counting them into one
#   matrix would imply a comparison the design does not support.
